A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same patchification-scaling study. All 13 pages of each version, including Figures 1–4, Tables 1–10 and Appendix A, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, segmentation and detection experiments on ImageNet-1k, ADE20k and COCO, together with scaling and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and ablation results reported in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same ViT/Adventurer patch-size scaling procedure, classification token, detection decoder and linear-layer alternative to the segmentation decoder. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ImageNet-1k classification, ADE20k semantic segmentation, and COCO detection and instance segmentation tasks. The added Pixel Transformer discussion concerns prior work, not additional evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged, including DeiT/Adventurer configurations, UperNet versus linear segmentation heads, and token interpolation versus patch-size scaling. Newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same metrics, model configurations, training schedules, hyperparameters and memory/runtime estimation protocol. The new aggregate compute disclosure does not report a revised experimental budget.

E4.justification: The decoder comparison, parameter-scaling comparison, input-resolution analysis, joint scaling study and sequence-interpolation ablation are retained without substantive revisions in Figures 2–4 and Tables 4–5.

E5.justification: The single-run wording in Section 4.3 and shaded plots in Figure 1 are unchanged. v2 adds no seed information, repeated-run statistics, confidence-interval reporting or significance tests.

E6.justification: The experimental tables and figures retain the same entries, values and trends. Examples include 84.6% ImageNet accuracy for pixel-tokenized Adventurer-Base and 46.8 mIoU for decoder-free Adventurer-Base with 2×2 patches.

T1.justification: The encoder and tokenization definitions in Section 3.1 remain unchanged. Neither version supplies additional formal assumptions, scaling-law derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: smaller patches improve performance, pixel tokenization supports 50,176-token sequences and 84.6% ImageNet accuracy, and smaller patches reduce the benefit of segmentation decoders.

C2.justification: The information-loss explanation, decoder interpretation, and computational and input-resolution limitations remain unchanged. The added Impact Statement provides resource disclosure and broad societal commentary without a substantive new scientific explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: The new Impact Statement discloses approximately 50,000 A100 GPU hours for the experiments. Previously documented implementation details, Appendix A training recipes, resource-estimation procedures and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Rejuvenating i-GPT, SCLIP, M-VAR and ViT-Linearizer. It also adds a brief discussion of Pixel Transformers as prior pixel-scale work, already cited in v1's Appendix A; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short related-work passage, an Impact Statement, funding acknowledgments and conference/correspondence information. The displayed author list removes Guoyizhe Wei. Most prose and the scientific section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Affiliations move to a first-page footnote, and text and floats reflow: Figure 4 moves between columns and Table 4 moves from page 7 to page 8. Figures and tables retain their designs, axes, legends and substantive captions.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency through the total compute disclosure and gives readers better main-text context for prior pixel-level modeling work. The methods, empirical evidence, claims and detailed appendix remain unchanged, so these benefits are limited.
